prompt: Reverse a list at the level of chunks rather than single items: the last chunk comes first, but the items inside each chunk keep their order. Complete reverseChunks.
explanation: The trick is to reverse the outer order while leaving the inner order alone, which a plain reverse would not do. Walking the chunk starts from the last one backwards and copying each chunk forwards achieves exactly that; the last chunk is the one most likely to be short, so its end has to be clamped to the list size. A chunk size of 1 degenerates into an ordinary reverse, which is a useful sanity check on your loop bounds.
hints: Work out where the last chunk starts first: it is the largest multiple of chunkSize that is still below items.size().
Step the outer loop backwards by chunkSize, and inside it copy elements FORWARDS so the order within a chunk is preserved.
Clamp the end of each chunk with Math.min(start + chunkSize, items.size()) so the short final chunk does not read past the end.
